answer: The protocol validates 1,000 unique location proofs by measuring signal transit across a willow grid. An issuer assigns spatial coordinates as a timber anchor, and each signed receipt proves an agent occupied the site. A verifier reproduces failure by re-running logs, mapping any ocean latency discrepancy to trigger a penalty. Honest nodes pay linear physical travel costs, while 1,000 fakes incur unsustainable signal congestion.
